summary: Iteration 99 was the closing retest of FIX 1-5 plus the final money sweep. It covered the backend only, as requested. REGRESSION: test_jun2026_owner_batch passed 13/13, test_jun2026_recharge_and_settlement 16/16, test_iter96_fixes 11/11 and test_iter98_advance_recovery 11/11. Under pytest, test_iter96_reconciliation, test_iter97_returns_outstanding, test_iter97_recharge_notify and test_iter97_concurrency gave 12 passed and 1 skipped (the 5/hour settlement limit, even after a backend restart), and test_iter98_final_batch passed 7/7 when rerun once the login limit of 10 per minute had cleared. NEW suite tests/test_iter99_closing.py: 12 passed, 1 failed. FIX 1 VERIFIED with a real short-seller flow, not a seeded row. A ₹200 return where the seller held ₹50 raised vendor_receivable by exactly 150. The admin list showed advance_outstanding 150 and cashback_outstanding 0. One tap gave advance_applied 150, the wallet went 500→350 and the row settled with recovered=150. Receivables fell by 150, there was exactly 1 advance_recovery debit row, a replay returned 400 and took nothing, and replaying refund-from-company did not reopen the row (Δ0). Four parallel HTTP recoveries returned [200,400,400,400]: ₹200 was taken once, the wallet dropped by exactly 200, there was 1 txn and no row had recovered > amount. An 8-way in-process race held the same invariants (row recovered = wallet debit = treasury credit). A partial recovery (₹100 of ₹300) followed by next-sale auto recovery took the remaining ₹200 once under the ADVRECOVER key, and replaying that sale took nothing. With both kinds owed, cashback was cleared first (40) and then the advance (30). FIX 2 VERIFIED: the script reported 'closed 0, kept 2' and kept both a genuinely parked row and a row whose return does not exist. FIX 3 VERIFIED: all 49 rejected withdrawals with a fee have exactly 1 WDL_FEEBACK, 1 WDLFEEREV_REJECT reversal and at most 1 collection row, no seller was credited twice, and group_1 platform_fee 17.82 = fee rows 6289.82 − reversals 6272. FIX 4 is PARTIAL. The API breakdown sums exactly to ledger_balance 6252.5, which equals available, and in_sync and balanced are true. The LEDGERFIX row (vendor_adjustment_debit ₹6,716) is clearly described and appears in the vendor and admin exports. However, the Excel 'Reconciliation' sheet still lists only the old lines: they sum to −233,390.5 against a ledger balance of 6,252.5 (FAIL). FIX 5 VERIFIED: an open delivery_fee row adds +33 to vendor_receivable; kinds [] with networks airtel and tata-play comes back as kinds ['dth','mobile'] with both operators; the seller notice reads 'recharge of <number> is in progress/done' and never 'shipped'. MONEY SWEEP: there are no duplicate (type, user, ref) groups across all 55 ledger types (including advance_recovery and the LEDGERFIX adjustment) and no duplicate idempotency keys. No debit row lacks a remark and no row has both a debit and a credit. Receivables (0) tie to the open vendor_outstanding rows (0). Both the admin group-wise export (22 sheets, including Recharge) and the vendor export open. NEW BUGS: (1) HIGH: delivery_fee outstanding rows are not keyed or closed. Re-delivering a short seller's order creates a second open ₹20 row, and when the fee is later actually paid both rows stay open, so with FIX 5 the seller would be charged the fee 3 times. (2) FIXTURE POLLUTION: testvendor has ₹675 of advance_recovery debits with no funded advance behind them, and ₹5,840 of cashback_recovery against only ₹2,620 of backing cashback rows, all from test suites seeding fake debts on the real account. (3) The legacy cashback_vendor_recovery UPI rows still show as Credits in the Vendor Wallet sheet, and new types fall into the Slangcart Treasury sheet by default.

critical.issue: When the seller is short, vendor_outstanding kind=delivery_fee is written with insert_one, which is not keyed. Moving the order delivered→shipped→delivered while still short creates a SECOND open ₹20 row for the same order, so Receivables show ₹40 for a ₹20 fee. When the seller later has money and the order is re-delivered, delivery_charge_paid is debited, but both open rows stay open. Now that FIX 5 counts delivery_fee as a receivable and vendor_advances recovers it, the seller would pay ₹20 + ₹40. Reproduced with tests/iter99_delivery_fee_retry_probe.py.

minor.issue: The sheet still lists only Opening, Sales, Delivery charges, Refunds, Withdrawals, Cashback funded, Adjustments and Other. It omits Sale reversals (430), Withdrawal reversals (246,458), Delivery reversals (30), Recoveries (6,415), Transaction fees (6,272) and Fee refunds (6,272). Its lines sum to −233,390.5 while '= Ledger balance' shows 6,252.5, so the owner still sees a sheet that does not add up, even though 'Balanced: YES'. The API reconciliation.formula text also omits recoveries and fees.

_unclaim restores recovered to the stale 'was' value. If another claimer advanced the same row in between, and this call's debit then fails (InsufficientFunds), the other claimer's recovery is wiped and the row shows as owed again although its wallet was debited, which allows a double recovery. Use $inc {recovered: -take} and reopen the row instead.

A racer that loses the optimistic update skips the row instead of re-reading it. In the 8-way race, one run recovered only 150 of the 200 owed, and a follow-up call took the remaining 50. No money is lost, but parallel calls under-collect.

The top-level rows, outstanding_before and outstanding_after are cashback-only (0 / 0.0 when only an advance was recovered). In the mixed case the response says unapplied: 60 when only 30 was unapplied (100 asked, 70 applied). Recompute these after the advance step.

Types not listed in GROUPS fall into 'Slangcart Treasury' by default: advance_recovery, vendor_adjustment_debit (LEDGERFIX), withdrawal_transaction_fee_refund, reversal, opening_balance, manual_adjustment_*, legacy_reconcile_inflow and phone_reveal_fee. advance_recovery belongs in 'Vendor Outstanding' next to cashback_recovery, and the fee refund and fee reversal belong in 'Vendor Settlement'. In the Treasury sheet, recoveries (money in) appear in the Debit column.

Still open from iteration 98: the legacy cashback_vendor_recovery UPI rows TXNA208, TXNA1295 and TXNA1514 (₹30, ₹30, ₹40) appear as Credits in the Vendor Wallet sheet, although they never touched the vendor wallet.

action_items: HIGH: in shop_money.settle_delivery_fee, upsert the delivery_fee outstanding row keyed on (order_id, kind). When the fee is later debited successfully, close that open row (or skip the debit and let vendor_advances recover it), so one fee can never be both paid and recovered.

Add the missing lines to the vendor Excel Reconciliation sheet so it sums to '= Ledger balance': Sale reversals, Withdrawal reversals, Delivery reversals, Cashback funding returned, Recoveries, Transaction fees and Fee refunds. Update reconciliation.formula to match.

Fixture hygiene: test_iter98_advance_recovery.py and test_iter97_concurrency.py (and the older cashback suites) seed fake debts on the REAL testvendor and recover them from his real wallet. That has left ₹675 of advance_recovery with no funded advance (₹450 credited to shopping_margin, ₹225 to a no-op bucket) and ₹5,840 of cashback_recovery against only ₹2,620 of backing rows. Move these suites to isolated TEST_ vendors with teardown, or use the real funding flow (refund-from-company). Decide whether to post a one-time labelled correction for testvendor.
In vendor_advances._unclaim, use $inc {recovered: -take} instead of restoring the stale value.
Fix the recover response fields (rows, outstanding_before/after, unapplied) so they cover both cashback and advances.

Map advance_recovery to 'Vendor Outstanding', withdrawal_transaction_fee_refund and reversal to 'Vendor Settlement', and vendor_adjustment_* to an Adjustments group in wallet_export.GROUPS, instead of the Treasury fallback. Fix the direction of the legacy cashback_vendor_recovery rows in the Vendor Wallet sheet.
critical_code_review_comments: vendor_advances._claim filters on 'recovered': row.get('recovered') or 0, which does not match rows where the field is absent. Every current writer sets recovered=0.0, but a legacy or hand-made row without the field would never be claimable.
returns.py: replaying the company-funded upsert after recovery correctly keeps the row settled (verified Δ0), because the RETURNCOMPANY key gates the path.
server.py (>8000 lines), core/cashback.py (972) and routes/vendor_networth.py (695) are well past the 700-line guideline.

rca_of_issue: Delivery fee: settle_delivery_fee's InsufficientFunds branch calls db.vendor_outstanding.insert_one (not keyed) and does not set delivery_settled, so every later delivered transition retries the fee. A retry while still short adds another row. A retry with money debits the fee, but nothing closes the open rows. Reproduction: an order with dp_id and delivery_charge 20, seller wallet 0 → delivered (1 open row) → shipped → delivered (2 open rows) → wallet set to 100 → shipped → delivered (delivery_charge_paid=1, wallet 80, both rows still open). Excel reconciliation: the _sheet('Reconciliation') call in vendor_networth.py lines 592-607 was not updated when the breakdown gained its new keys.
